hook: Possessing the strength of twenty men, Count Dracula remains a terrifying figure in Bram Stoker's novel.

sections.voiceover: Possessing the strength of twenty men, Count Dracula remains a terrifying figure in Bram Stoker's novel.

sections.voiceover: In the Carpathian Mountains, Abraham Van Helsing identifies the vampire as a former, devil-dealing necromancer. Does human logic provide a defense against a creature with the strength of twenty men?
sections.visual_cue: A map of the Carpathian Mountains transitioning to a classic magnifying glass over a Victorian document.

sections.voiceover: Author Loren D. Estleman raised the stakes in his 1978 pastiche, Sherlock Holmes vs. Dracula.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a vintage 1978 book cover design with bold, period-appropriate typography.

sections.voiceover: This 1978 novel pits the detective against the vampire's strength of twenty men. Sherlock Holmes relies on his human logic to survive the vampire's strength of twenty men.
sections.visual_cue: An abstract split-screen showing a brain diagram on one side and a dark, mystical swirling mist on the other.

sections.voiceover: The Carpathian Mountains remain the home of the Count and his twenty-man strength.
